teams.heading: Jake White faces Japan this weekend in first match after appointment
teams.body: Jake White's first match in charge is against Japan this weekend, a side that beat Fiji 20-15 in the Pacific Nations Cup. White inherits a team ranked 10th in the world that has lost four of five Tests this year, and the 2027 World Cup in Australia is only a year away. Pool C at that tournament pairs Fiji with Argentina, Canada and Spain.

lead.why: It carries the freshest match-specific facts in the pack: White's first match in charge is against Japan this weekend.

teams.heading: Tom Pearson, England's injured flanker, back training and close to Prem return
teams.body: Northampton boss Phil Dowson said on Tuesday that Tom Pearson, the one-time England flanker, is back training with the squad. Dowson said it won't be long before Pearson is back out there, but there is no confirmation he will be ready for Saturday's match against Leicester Tigers. For England, the club's Champions Cup quartet of Manny Iyogun, Alex Coles, Henry Pollock and Tommy Freeman are expected to return this weekend, while Dowson has found the scrum-half choice between Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland difficult.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item in the pack, with named England players and a Northampton injury update that bears on selection.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos to miss France's entire autumn Nations Championship with thigh setback
teams.body: Thomas Ramos will miss all four of France's autumn Nations Championship matches, according to L'Equipe, after a thigh injury first picked up in September was aggravated on his return to training. France have decided to rest the fullback for the rest of the autumn rather than risk making the problem worse. His absence also removes their main goal kicker, whose tee accuracy proved vital in the 2026 Six Nations, including the winning penalty against England.

lead.why: Ramos's autumn absence is the biggest new France men's team fact in the pack, and it removes their main goal kicker.

teams.heading: Farrell to name Nations Championship squad today as Caelan Doris remains sidelined
teams.body: Andy Farrell names his Ireland squad for the Nations Championship on Wednesday afternoon, with captain Caelan Doris still sidelined and Jack Conan's injury from last Saturday adding to the loss. The bigger news is the return of Andrew Porter, Ryan Baird and Mack Hansen, who have not played for Ireland since the final game of last November's series against South Africa. Ireland meet Argentina, Fiji and South Africa at the Aviva Stadium, then a play-off at Twickenham.

lead.why: The highest-scoring new item, and the squad announcement lands today with named returnees and absentees.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa at home in November 2025
teams.body: Italy's last meeting with South Africa was a home defeat, 32-14 in November 2025 in an international friendly. That is a single result, not a head-to-head record, so it tells us little about the wider pattern between the sides. The sharper numbers come from the log: across three Nations Championship matches, Italy have scored 37 points and conceded 131, with no wins.

teams.heading: Former Scotland captain Stuart Hogg stripped of MBE after domestic abuse conviction
teams.body: King Charles removed the MBE from former Scotland captain Stuart Hogg in March, after Hogg pleaded guilty to a domestic abuse charge involving his estranged wife. The honour, awarded in the 2024 New Year Honours for services to rugby, is one of 15 revoked in 2026 according to the Cabinet Office's official register. Hogg won 100 caps for Scotland and toured three times with the British & Irish Lions, but his career achievements were overshadowed by the conviction.

lead.why: A men's Scotland story with a named former captain, and the one fresh item in the shortlist that is not women's or club news.

teams.heading: Tandy keeps Taulupe Faletau in World Cup frame after November omission
teams.body: Steve Tandy has left the door open for Taulupe Faletau to push for next year's World Cup in Australia, despite the 35-year-old's omission from the 39-man Nations Championship squad. Faletau returned from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton, playing 55 minutes, and has 109 Wales caps but has not played under Tandy. "He is a legend of our game and a world-class player, so we would definitely not rule anyone out," Tandy said.

teams.heading: Frans Malherbe recalls soldiering on with broken leg in Pumas Test
teams.body: Springbok prop Frans Malherbe has shared the story of soldiering on with a broken leg during a 2014 Rugby Championship Test against Los Pumas in Argentina, in a video posted by SA Rugby Magazine. The Rugby Championship is not being played this year, but Argentina did meet South Africa in August, losing 17-10 to the Springboks in a match where the Pumas' ferocious defence earned credit. Malherbe's story is a reminder of how physical that rivalry has long been.

teams.heading: Women's WXV: Aicha Sutcliffe makes first Scotland start against Wallaroos in Canberra
teams.body: Dave Butcher, Scotland's interim head coach, has named Glasgow hooker Aicha Sutcliffe to start in one of three changes for the women's final WXV Global Series match against the Wallaroos in Canberra. It is Sutcliffe's third straight match against Australia's women, after a 56-12 defeat in Sydney, and Scotland are still seeking their first win of the competition. Sarah Bonar returns in the second row after missing that game through illness.

lead.why: The only new item with a concrete squad decision not already run, and it touches the Wallaroos.

teams.heading: Japan women's sevens retain Asia Rugby Emirates Series title in Colombo
teams.body: Japan's women's sevens side retained the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series title in Colombo, going undefeated across the leg and beating China 14-7 in the final. Japan's men's sevens also won the Colombo leg, beating Hong Kong China 28-14 in the final. The women's squad now turns its attention to HSBC SVNS in Dubai at the end of November.

teams.heading: Kieran Read expects Damian McKenzie back at full-back once Richie Mo'unga recovers
teams.body: Damian McKenzie's fly-half spell may not last. Kieran Read expects him back at full-back once Richie Mo'unga recovers from a calf injury, even after McKenzie started at 10 in both Bledisloe Cup Tests against Australia. Justin Marshall, on The Good, The Bad & Rugby podcast, believes the November Tests against Scotland, Wales and England will be tougher, with wetter conditions and more static ball, but calls McKenzie "one of the most dangerous rugby players in the world".

lead.why: It is the highest-scoring new item, it has not been run, and it names McKenzie and a live question about his position.

teams.heading: Springbok Dan du Preez ruled out of Bath's next two Premiership matches
teams.body: Springbok back-rower Dan du Preez has been ruled out of Bath's next two Premiership matches after tearing a hamstring in training before their Investec Champions Cup defeat to Montpellier. Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan said the injury will keep the 31-year-old out for "a considerable amount of time". Du Preez joined Bath from Sale Sharks this season and has made two appearances, scoring two tries.

lead.why: A concrete injury to a Springbok is the strongest new item in the pack, ahead of commentary and the already-run Sharks and Kwagga Smith stories.
